problem: Households paying part-time domestic help informally (notebook/memory) have month-end disputes over days worked and wages owed, with the leading app in this niche drifting from offline-only toward requiring a Google account
target_user: Urban/semi-urban Indian households employing part-time domestic staff (maid/cook/driver), managed by the household budget-keeper

evidence.claim: ServiceBook is free, tracks attendance (Hajiri) and advances (Udhari), auto-calculates salary, and markets itself as fully offline
ServiceBook version 3.1.3 added 'Smart Cloud Backup' via Google Sign-In, moving away from its original no-cloud posture
MaidCircle (iOS) implements attendance -> auto salary calculation, advances/loans tracking, and digital payment history, but has limited reviews
Homemaid handles overtime, days worked, vacations, absences, and monthly payments for domestic employees
No competitor found in this search advertises a Hindi/regional-language UI or a continuous mid-month running-balance view; all appear to calculate salary at month-end only
A closely related niche (offline, no-account, no-ads bill splitting) is already served by at least 7 established Google Play competitors, one with 100,000+ installs

complaints: INFERRED: month-end disputes over exact days worked/amount owed when tracking is informal (notebook/memory) — the entire premise every competitor in this niche is independently built to solve
VERIFIED_FACT: the category's most visible incumbent now asks for a Google account for its newer backup feature, despite marketing itself as offline/private
requested_features: ESTIMATE: regional-language (Hindi) UI — inferred from target-user demographics, not from a specific user request found in research
ESTIMATE: a running/continuous balance rather than an end-of-month-only calculation
proposed_solution: A small offline-only Android app ('Hisaab') for tracking one or more household staff members' daily attendance, advances, and a continuously up-to-date wage balance, with a Hindi/English toggle and zero account requirement enforced by never requesting the INTERNET permission.
differentiation: No INTERNET permission requested at all — a technically verifiable no-account, no-cloud guarantee, directly answering the trust gap opened by the leading competitor's move to Google Sign-In
Continuous mid-month running balance view instead of end-of-month-only calculation
Hindi + English UI toggle from v1, addressing a localization gap no found competitor advertises
Local file export/import for backup, preserving user convenience without a cloud account
